parts.name: Vertical-speed indicator case and bezel
parts.description: United reference envelope: 3.248 in typical flange width; case depth shown at the published maximum (2.30 in ASI, 4.0 in altimeter/VSI). Unspecified diameters and features are reconstructed. Internal reference mechanisms come from separate sources; this is not a complete United replica.

parts.name: Vertical-speed indicator indicating element
parts.description: Readable teaching indicator driven from the shared demonstration state.

parts.name: Vertical-speed indicator corrugated diaphragm stack
parts.description: Reconstructed from Vertical-speed indicator mechanism-layout drawings; exact proportions and dimensions are inferred. Circular corrugated diaphragm faces lie in the x/y plane and stack along the depth axis.

parts.name: Vertical-speed indicator capsule clevis
parts.description: Reconstructed from Vertical-speed indicator mechanism-layout drawings; exact proportions and dimensions are inferred. Paired clevis cheeks and cross-pin transfer membrane displacement to the connecting link. Travel is visually amplified.

parts.name: Vertical-speed indicator moving transmission link
parts.description: Reconstructed from Vertical-speed indicator mechanism-layout drawings; exact proportions and dimensions are inferred. Pinned connecting link follows capsule displacement and the sector lever. Kinematic travel is illustrative, not calibrated.

parts.name: Vertical-speed indicator rocking shaft
parts.description: Reconstructed from Vertical-speed indicator mechanism-layout drawings; exact proportions and dimensions are inferred. Bridge and rocking shaft transfer diaphragm motion to the sector.

parts.name: Vertical-speed indicator sector gear
parts.description: Reconstructed from Vertical-speed indicator mechanism-layout drawings; exact proportions and dimensions are inferred. Partial toothed sector keeps the linkage within the .375-radius reconstructed case envelope.

parts.name: Vertical-speed indicator handstaff pinion
parts.description: Reconstructed from Vertical-speed indicator mechanism-layout drawings; exact proportions and dimensions are inferred. Small reduction pinion between sector and centered indicating shaft.

parts.name: Vertical-speed indicator pointer shaft
parts.description: Reconstructed from Vertical-speed indicator mechanism-layout drawings; exact proportions and dimensions are inferred. Indicating shaft is centered on the dial axis.

parts.name: Vertical-speed indicator pointer linkage
parts.description: Reconstructed from Vertical-speed indicator mechanism-layout drawings; exact proportions and dimensions are inferred. Linkage ends at the centered pointer shaft.

parts.name: Vertical-speed indicator hairspring
parts.description: Reconstructed from Vertical-speed indicator mechanism-layout drawings; exact proportions and dimensions are inferred. Planar spiral hairspring supplies restoring force around the linkage.

parts.name: Vertical-speed indicator shaft bearing
parts.description: Reconstructed from Vertical-speed indicator mechanism-layout drawings; exact proportions and dimensions are inferred. Jewel-like bearing at the centered shaft.

parts.name: VSI rear static inlet line
parts.description: Reconstructed from Vertical-speed indicator mechanism-layout drawings; exact proportions and dimensions are inferred. Connects the rear static fitting to the diaphragm/capillary branch point.

parts.name: VSI direct static to diaphragm
parts.description: Reconstructed from Vertical-speed indicator mechanism-layout drawings; exact proportions and dimensions are inferred. Unrestricted static path enters the diaphragm. The case receives static through a separate calibrated capillary.

parts.name: VSI porcelain capillary to case
parts.description: Reconstructed from Vertical-speed indicator mechanism-layout drawings; exact proportions and dimensions are inferred. Thin-walled porcelain capillary vents the surrounding case to the static inlet. The bore size is unverified.

sources.title: 7000 Series Vertical Speed Indicators
sources.use: Public product description/specification links for the 7000 series. Use 7000 for VSI; 7100 is a different instantaneous VSI series.
sources.locator: 7000 Series section and linked specification sheets; keep separate from 7100 Series.

sources.title: Indicator-Rate of Climb, United Instruments Spec. No. UI7000 (revision F)
sources.use: Best OEM exterior-envelope and performance source found for an actual conventional United mechanical VSI/rate-of-climb family; pair with Army Figure 4-12 only as generic internal architecture, not as the UI7000's confirmed internals.
locator: PDF p.4, OEM drawing: dimensioned face and side views for UI7000-series configurations, with case per MS33549 and 1/8-27 ANPT ports per MIL-P-7105.
PDF p.1 describes pressure-difference operation, single pointer, range and zero setting; PDF pp.2-3 provide performance/tolerance criteria.

sources.title: Aviation Unit Maintenance (AVUM) and Aviation Intermediate Maintenance (AVIM) Manual for General Aircraft Maintenance, Electrical and Instrument Maintenance Procedures and Practices, Volume 4, TM 1-1500-204-23-4
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of the Army / LOGSA; hosted by Chinook Helicopter public technical-manual archive
sources.use: Best primary-source public mechanical layout for conventional ASI and VSI behavior; not a matched component overhaul manual and not usable for dimensional reconstruction.
locator: PDF p.62, printed p.4-13, Figure 4-11: sectional airspeed-indicator drawing labels static/pitot connections, diaphragm, restraining spring, hairspring, rocking shaft, sector, long lever, handstaff pinion and pointer. Adjacent text describes capsule motion converted to pointer movement by mechanical linkage.

PDF p.63, printed p.4-14, text: conventional VSI includes two air-enclosing chambers, with a pressure-sensitive diaphragm directly connected to static pressure and an airtight case connected through a thin-walled porcelain capillary; diaphragm motion drives the pointer. This is source text rather than inference.

PDF p.64, printed p.4-15, Figure 4-12: conventional VSI sectional layout with internal diaphragm/chamber, mechanical linkage and case/capillary path. It is a section/layout view, not an exploded parts drawing.
PDF p.63, printed p.4-14, Table 4-1 gives ASI test tolerance values for MS28045/MS28021/MS28046 at specified knots. Those are performance limits, not physical dimensions.
